I farm only 8 mu, and my family has people working off-farm, so I will keep the plan simple, steady, and labor-saving. Because my main system is wheat-maize and I have well irrigation, I will put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation and keep a smaller piece for cotton. I will use better seed on all three crops because I need stable yield more than low upfront cost. I will not push fertilizer and water to the maximum; I will use moderate inputs that I can manage myself and that fit local conditions. For wheat, I will focus on stable winter survival, enough base fertilizer, and a few irrigations at key stages. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, more nitrogen than wheat, and fewer irrigations because summer rain helps. For cotton, I will keep only a small area because it takes more labor, but I will still plant it for income diversification. I will use rotary tillage or no-tillage where it saves work, and I will keep pesticide use at a moderate level, applying it when I think pest and disease pressure justifies it. My goal this year is not to chase the highest yield. I will aim for steady production, manageable labor, and lower risk.
